native.command: scripts/qws/aka-run formats --x86-64-v2 -- cargo test --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p proseql-storage --test streaming_readers -- --nocapture
native.note: Buffer capacities, not process RSS. The scan bound includes two host buffers during replacement and both framer buffers. Interrupted durable-replacement recovery now uses fixed-size buffers too; see recovery evidence below.

recovery.command: scripts/qws/aka-run formats --x86-64-v2 -- cargo test --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p proseql-storage --test streaming_recovery -- --nocapture
recovery.note: Tests both stat and a two-byte range read with absent, PENDING and 100 MiB malformed markers. Identical destination/backup bytes preserve the destination inode; different same-size bytes restore the backup inode. A counting allocator measures all requested heap bytes during each recovery. Existing recovery outcomes and cleanup remain unchanged.

chromium.command: scripts/qws/aka-run formats -- bash -c 'bun run --cwd packages/engine build:wasm && bun run tsc --build && node packages/engine/scripts/measure-browser-blob-scan.mjs'
chromium.path: File -> Blob.slice.arrayBuffer -> WASM shared RowSource (not query execution)
chromium.note: Chromium precise performance.memory, sampled every 1024 rows. Initial and final explicit GC use CDP. The one-second value is before the final GC. Selected source File is disk-backed, not loaded in full.

node.command: scripts/qws/aka-run formats -- bash -c 'bun run --cwd packages/engine build:wasm && bun run tsc --build && node --expose-gc packages/engine/scripts/measure-blob-scan.mjs'
node.path: openAsBlob -> Blob.slice.arrayBuffer -> WASM shared RowSource (not query execution)

limits: Raw-row framing evidence, not browser query/executor parity or lazy-partition support.
Framer memory scales with chunk size plus the longest physical line.
Each JS callback receives owned row bytes. GC and process RSS do not have the native reusable-buffer bound.
Chromium retained more JS heap after one second than before the scan. Node retained RSS after explicit GC. No back-to-idle claim.
The future browser executor should consume rows inside Rust and return only query results to avoid per-row JS allocations.
